question: Why do we do shift handovers on the ward?

options.A: To replace formal patient case note documentation
options.B: To maintain continuity of patient care and safety
options.C: To complete daily hospital administrative audits
options.D: To socialise with incoming colleagues before work

explanation: Handover makes sure the incoming team gets all the important details they need to keep patients safe without any gaps in care. You've got this! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why should a clinical handover avoid reading entire patient case notes word-for-word?

options.A: Case notes are strictly confidential and cannot be opened during shifts
options.B: It prevents the doctor from writing new prescriptions
options.C: Incoming nurses are legally barred from reading past medical histories
options.D: It wastes time and obscures urgent, current clinical priorities

explanation: Good handover focuses on what is happening right now and recent changes, rather than rereading old history that is already written down in the chart. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h1)

question: When giving a patient report during handover, what is the most important thing to say first?

options.A: The total cost of hospital bills
options.C: The name of the attending consultant

explanation: Starting with who the patient is and their main diagnosis makes sure everyone is immediately on the same page about who is being discussed. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h2)

question: You are handing over a new mother who just had a severe postpartum hemorrhage. Which detail is a must-include for safety?

options.A: Current lochia amount and recent vital signs trend
options.B: The brand of sanitary pads preferred by the patient
options.C: The maiden name of the patient's grandmother
options.D: The exact menu the patient ate for lunch

explanation: Bleeding and vital signs are key clues that tell the incoming shift if the patient is stable or at risk for shock. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h2)

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
explanation: A stands for Assessment—your professional view of what is going on with the patient right now. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h3)

question: When a midwife uses the 'Recommendation' part of SBAR during a call to a doctor, what is she doing?

options.A: Handing over her personal shift duties to the medical officer
options.B: Stating clearly what action or medication she wants for the patient
options.C: Asking the doctor to guess what is wrong with the patient
options.D: Reporting the exact time the patient was admitted to the ward

explanation: The recommendation step removes ambiguity by explicitly proposing what intervention is needed next. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h3)

question: What must always go with a patient when transferring them from your ward to another department?

options.A: Cash deposit receipts for upcoming procedures
options.B: A clear verbal handover and written transfer documentation
options.C: A signed permission letter from the hospital director
options.D: All physical bed sheets used during their admission

explanation: Safe transfers need both a good talk (verbal) and good paperwork to keep the care flowing smoothly. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h4)

question: You need to transfer an unstable eclamptic patient to the intensive care unit. What is your most important first step?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the official visiting hours
options.B: Packing the patient's personal traveling bags first
options.C: Discharging the patient formally from the hospital register
options.D: Ensuring the ICU is ready and the patient is stabilized for transit

explanation: Always make sure the patient is stable enough to travel and the receiving unit is fully ready for them before moving them. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is a major plus of doing shift handover right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to write formal notes
options.B: It completely removes the risk of hospital-acquired infections
options.C: It allows the patient to hear, correct, and participate in their care plan
options.D: It stops doctors from visiting patients during morning rounds

explanation: Bedside handover puts the patient right at the center, letting them speak up and help clear up any mix-ups immediately. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h5)

question: How should a midwife handle private test results during a bedside handover?

options.A: Discuss sensitive personal matters with lowered voice and discretion
options.B: Shout the results across the ward so everyone learns from them
options.C: Refuse to mention any clinical findings while in the patient room
options.D: Ask visitors to leave the hospital premises entirely during shift change

explanation: Bedside handovers are great, but we must always keep our voices down to protect patient dignity and privacy. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h5)

question: What does a 'blind handover' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Reporting patient vital signs without using a thermometer
options.B: Accepting a shift report without physically verifying the patient's condition
options.C: Reading patient reports in a completely dark room
options.D: Handing over patients while wearing protective eye goggles

explanation: A blind handover is a big safety risk because you are taking charge of patients you haven't even gone to see with your own eyes. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h6)

question: When does professional responsibility for a patient officially shift to the incoming nursing team?

options.A: When the handover is completed and accepted by the incoming staff
options.B: Only after the hospital medical director signs the monthly roster
options.C: As soon as the morning sun rises over the hospital ward
options.D: When the patient's relatives pay their hospital admission fees

explanation: Responsibility moves over as soon as the incoming team receives, understands, and accepts the full patient report. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h6)
